note.after_visit_summary: Your diabetes is not at goal right now, with an A1c of 8.4%. This is likely because you stopped glipizide two months ago after having low blood sugar (your sugar went down to 62). We will stop glipizide so you do not have more low sugars. You will keep taking metformin 1000 mg twice a day with breakfast and dinner. You will start a new pill called empagliflozin 10 mg once daily in the morning. It is a pill, not a shot. Drink plenty of water and keep the genital area clean. If you get itching or a yeast infection, call us. If you are sick and cannot eat or drink, skip the pill that day. You are allergic to sulfa (Bactrim), which caused a whole-body rash. We sent a referral for a diabetes eye exam; our office will email the details to lupe rios 65 at example dot com. Keep walking in the evenings. Please check your blood sugar at home and bring the results. Repeat your A1c in 3 months. Return if you feel very low, cannot eat or drink, or have a yeast infection that does not get better.
